title: Repair NULL-sensitive exclusion in a deployment report
goal: As a software engineer supporting a fictional release team, I will repair a deployment eligibility query that incorrectly hides valid builds when an exclusion table contains a NULL build ID. In an 18–22 minute DBeaver workflow, I will inspect the small local tables, demonstrate SQL three-valued logic, choose an explicit policy for unknown IDs, replace the faulty NOT IN predicate with a correlated NOT EXISTS query, and verify exactly which builds the release maintainer can include. The substantive work is SQL correctness and edge-case reasoning in one app; the change is limited to one reporting query.
start: Before recording, a small fictional local SQLite database will be prepared with about ten builds and an exclusion table containing a matching ID, a duplicate ID and a NULL. A short faulty SELECT and independently enumerated expected IDs will be available. No corrected query or comparison output exists yet. No live database or production data is used.
result: In DBeaver, create the corrected SQL query with comments documenting the unknown-ID policy, and export a compact before/after result table identifying the eligible build IDs. The final decision explains why NOT IN loses rows in the presence of NULL and why the chosen correlated predicate implements the release rule.
verify: Compare returned build IDs against the independently enumerated expected set, not merely the row count. Run focused cases for a NULL exclusion entry, duplicate exclusion entries, an empty exclusion table, a matching exclusion, and an unknown build ID. Confirm duplicates do not multiply results, the stated unknown-ID policy holds, and the local input tables remain unchanged.
